sections.h2: Own taxes are about two rupees in every hundred of panchayat revenue

chart.title: Central grants alone supplied 69.9% of panchayat revenue in 2022-23
chart.sub: Share of total village panchayat revenue, 2022-23, %.

sections.means: Own taxes, mostly property tax, came to Rs 737 crore of the Rs 35,354 crore that reporting panchayats received.
sections.todo: Follow the committee's call for a strategy to raise own-source revenue, since the grants cover most of what panchayats spend.

sections.h2: Panchayat revenue shrank as a share of GDP between 2020-21 and 2022-23

chart.title: Panchayat revenue fell from 0.21% to 0.13% of GDP in two years
chart.sub: Panchayat revenue as a share of GDP, %.

sections.means: Spending fell from 0.13% to 0.08% of GDP over the same years, and average spending per panchayat fell from Rs 17.3 lakh to Rs 12.5 lakh.
sections.todo: Read the 2026-31 performance grant against this baseline before judging whether it changes the habit of raising own revenue.

sections.h2: The 16th Finance Commission award for 2026-31 is about 84% a year larger

chart.title: The 16th Finance Commission proposes Rs 435,236 crore, up from Rs 236,805 crore
chart.sub: Finance Commission recommendations for rural local bodies, Rs crore, for each award period.
chart.source: Finance Commission awards, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Of the 16th award, Rs 348,188 crore is a basic grant and Rs 87,048 crore is tied to performance.
sections.todo: Check how own-source revenue is measured before the performance grant is paid, because the RBI data show reporting is still incomplete.
